newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Boeing, CSA interested in Czech plane maker.
newsitem.headline: Boeing, CSA interested in Czech plane maker.

text.p: Boeing CO and Czech airline Ceske Aerolinie a.s. (CSA) on Monday said the two firms are still interested in forming a joint plan to buy into troubled military plane maker Aero Vodochody a.s..

Speaking at a news conference in Prague, Raymond Waldmann, Boeing senior vice-president for international issues, said Boeing representatives were in Prague to meet government representatives on the issue on Monday and Tuesday.
"We would like to proceed to a final solution in cooperation between CSA-Boeing which would be advantageous for both of us, and Aero Vodochody as well," said CSA general director Antonin Jakubse.

The Czech government has approved a restructuring plan for Aero, clearing it of extensive debts and cutting its basic capital, which would later be increased by a strategic partner which would get an about 34 percent stake.
Aero shareholders have so far failed to approve the plan.
He added that a strong foreign partner was Aero's only chance to survive on the competitive international market.
Jakubse said he "could imagine" that CSA and Boeing would split the offered Aero stake under a 50-50 scheme.
Waldmann said Boeing had evaluated Aero earlier as being financially too weak, but became more interested again after the government announced its restructuring plan.

"We are very much interested and we will proceed with further evaluation of Aero Vodochody's capabilities and in discussions with government officials to find out if Boeing business in the Czech Republic would be welcome," he said.
Industry and Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy has said that he would welcome a Czech partner for the plane maker.
Boeing officials said the firm's plans have not changed following its recently-announced merger with McDonnell-Douglas.
They ruled out that their interest in Aero would depend on the Czech army purchase of F-18 fighters offered by McDonnell-Douglas.

Aero is the largest domestic military equipment producer and with large export quotas and supplies to the army. The company is currently developing a light military training L-159 jet, equipped with avionics from U.S-based Rockwell Corp, which also is allied with Boeing.
The Czech army has promised to buy 72 of the upgraded jets. Dlouhy said the government would keep a minority stake in the company at least as long as the L-159s are produced.
